title: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A data set has values 4, 7, 9, 11, 14. What is the median?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(9\). Ordered: 4, 7, 9, 11, 14. Middle value = 9.

questions.q: Find the median of the data list \(11, 24, 15, 31, 18\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(18\). Sorted list is \(11, 15, 18, 24, 31\); middle value is \(18\).

questions.q: The mean of five quiz scores is \(84\). Four of the scores are \(78, 82, 86,\) and \(91\). What is the fifth score?
What is the range of the measurements \(42, 19, 67, 28, 53\)?

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: For what value of \( k \) will the lines \( 3x - ky = 12 \) and \( 2x + 6y = 15 \) be perpendicular?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 1. Slope of second line: \( 2x + 6y = 15 \implies y = -\dfrac{1}{3}x + 2.5 \implies m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{3} \). The perpendicular slope is \( m_1 = 3 \). First line: \( ky = 3x - 12 \implies m_1 = \dfrac{3}{k} \). Set \( \dfrac{3}{k} = 3 \implies k = 1 \).

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: If \( \dfrac{a}{b} = 2 \) and \( \dfrac{c}{b} = 5 \), what is the value of \( \dfrac{2a + 3c}{b} \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 19. Split the numerator: \( \dfrac{2a + 3c}{b} = 2\left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{c}{b}\right) = 2(2) + 3(5) = 4 + 15 = 19 \).

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The table shows test scores for two classes. What is the positive difference between the medians?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(1\). Median A = 81; Median B = 82. Difference = 1.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The mean of \(4\) numbers is \(36\). When one more number, \(31\), is added to the set, what is the new mean of all \(5\) numbers?
When an outlier of \(95\) is appended to the list \(12, 14, 15, 16, 18\), by how many units does the median increase?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(0.5\). Original median \(15\); new 6-item list middle pair \((15, 16)\) gives median \(15.5\), increase \(0.5\).

questions.q: A random survey estimates \(62\%\) support for a library expansion with a margin of error of \(4\%\). What is the minimum plausible population percentage?
Adding \(12\) to every number in a dataset raises its mean from \(45\) to what new value?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(57\). Shifting every observation by \(+12\) shifts the mean by \(+12\): \(45 + 12 = 57\).

questions.q: Two data sets have identical values except the largest entry increases from \(30\) to \(60\) in Set B of \(6\) items. By how much does the mean of Set B exceed Set A?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(5\). Sum increases by \(30\) across \(6\) values, raising the mean by \(30 / 6 = 5\).

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The range of the data set {3, 7, 2, 9, 5, 8} is
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(7\). The range is the maximum value minus the minimum value: \(\text{Maximum} = 9\), \(\text{Minimum} = 2\), so \(\text{Range} = 9 - 2 = 7\).

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: If \( \dfrac{x + 8}{3} = 7 \), what is the value of \( x \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 13. Multiply both sides by 3: \( x + 8 = 21 \). Subtract 8 from both sides: \( x = 21 - 8 = 13 \).

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: If \( 3x + 2y = 19 \) and \( 2x + 3y = 16 \), what is the value of \( x + y \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 7. Add the two linear equations directly together: \( (3x + 2y) + (2x + 3y) = 19 + 16 \implies 5x + 5y = 35 \). Divide the entire equation by 5: \( x + y = 7 \).

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: For what value of \( k \) does the system \( 3x - 6y = 12 \) and \( 2x - ky = 8 \) have infinitely many solutions?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 4. For a linear system to have infinitely many solutions, the equations must be proportional. Notice that \( \dfrac{3}{2} \) is the ratio of the \( x \)-coefficients. For the constant terms, \( \dfrac{12}{8} = \dfrac{3}{2} \). Equating the ratio of the \( y \)-coefficients gives \( \dfrac{-6}{-k} = \dfrac{3}{2} \implies \dfrac{6}{k} = \dfrac{3}{2} \implies 3k = 12 \implies k = 4 \).

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: If \( 2(3x - 4) + 5(2 - x) = kx + 2 \) has infinitely many solutions for all real values of \( x \), what is the value of \( k \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** 1. Simplify the left side: \( 6x - 8 + 10 - 5x = x + 2 \). For the equation to be an identity true for all \( x \), the coefficient of \( x \) on the left must equal the coefficient of \( x \) on the right: \( x + 2 = kx + 2 \implies k = 1 \).

questions.q: A sample of \(8\) homes has a mean price of \(240\) thousand dollars, and a sample of \(12\) homes has a mean price of \(290\) thousand dollars. What is the combined mean price, in thousands of dollars?

A random poll of \(1,000\) residents finds \(43\%\) favor a park trail with a \(3\%\) margin of error. If the town has \(20,000\) residents, what is the upper plausible bound for residents favoring the trail?
In dataset \(\{6, 6, 8, x, 14\}\), the mode is \(6\) and the mean equals \(9\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(11\). Sum is \(5 \times 9 = 45\), so \(6 + 6 + 8 + x + 14 = 45 \Rightarrow x = 11\).

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Fluency (21–28)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A scientist measured the weekly rainfall in millimeters over seven weeks: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, and 20. What was the median weekly rainfall?
questions.answer: The middle value in this ordered list of 7 numbers is 11.

questions.q: Which statistic is least affected when one extremely large outlier is added to a skewed dataset?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Median. The median depends only on middle positions, resisting extreme outliers.

questions.q: Two datasets have the same mean of \(50\). Dataset X is \(\{49, 50, 50, 50, 51\}\) and Dataset Y is \(\{20, 35, 50, 65, 80\}\). Which has the larger standard deviation?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Dataset Y. Values in Dataset Y lie much farther from the mean of \(50\), giving larger standard deviation.

questions.q: Every value in a sample is multiplied by \(3\). How does the standard deviation change?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Multiplies by \(3\). Scaling all data by a positive factor \(c\) scales standard deviation by \(c\).

questions.q: For the list \(4, 8, 8, 10, 12, 18\), which statement compares mean and median accurately?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Mean is greater than median. Mean \(= 60 / 6 = 10\) and median \(= (8 + 10)/2 = 9\), so mean \(>\) median.

questions.q: A researcher wants to estimate average screen time among all \(2,400\) students at a high school. Which sample method produces the least bias?
choices: Surveying the first \(50\) students entering the library
Polling members of the computer club
Surveying \(150\) students selected randomly from the full school roster
questions.answer: **Answer:** Surveying \(150\) students selected randomly from the full school roster. Random selection from the entire target roster avoids convenience and voluntary-response bias.

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: A school selects a simple random sample of 50 students from a complete list of all enrolled students. What best describes this sampling method?
questions.answer: This method describes a simple random sample of the student body, which can reasonably represent the population.
choices: A simple random sample of the student body, which can reasonably represent the population
A sample with clear undercoverage bias

questions.target: One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error
questions.q: A researcher surveys every 10th customer who exits a grocery store on a randomly chosen day. What best describes this sampling method?
questions.answer: This method describes a systematic sample of store customers, which can reasonably represent the population.
choices: A systematic sample of store customers, which can reasonably represent the population
A sample with clear undercoverage bias

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A frequency table shows the number of siblings reported by 20 students. The results are shown in the table. What is the mode of the number of siblings?
questions.answer: The sibling count with the highest frequency (8 students) is 1.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The temperature in degrees Celsius over 5 days was: \(-2, 0, 4, 7, 11\). What was the median temperature?
questions.answer: Ordered list has middle value 4°C.

questions.q: Poll A surveys \(250\) random voters and Poll B surveys \(1,000\) random voters using the same question. How do their margins of error compare?
choices: Poll B has a smaller margin of error
Poll A has a smaller margin of error
Poll B has four times the margin of error
questions.answer: **Answer:** Poll B has a smaller margin of error. Larger random sample sizes yield smaller margins of error.

questions.q: A study randomly assigns \(80\) volunteers into two groups: Group 1 drinks green tea daily and Group 2 drinks water. What can the researchers reasonably conclude if Group 1 shows lower blood pressure?
choices: Drinking green tea caused the lower blood pressure for volunteers like these
Everyone in the country will respond identically
questions.answer: **Answer:** Drinking green tea caused the lower blood pressure for volunteers like these. Random assignment into treatment/control allows cause-and-effect inference among similar volunteers.

questions.q: A right-skewed distribution of home prices has median \(310\) thousand dollars and mean \(385\) thousand dollars. Which statement best explains this difference?
choices: A few very high-priced mansions pull the mean above the median
Most homes cost more than \(385\) thousand
Negative outliers pulled the median upward
The range must be less than \(75\)
questions.answer: **Answer:** A few very high-priced mansions pull the mean above the median. Upper outliers pull the arithmetic mean higher while leaving the median centered.

questions.q: Adding the constant \(20\) to every element of dataset \(S\) changes which statistic?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Mean. A uniform shift adds \(20\) to the mean and median while leaving measures of spread unchanged.

questions.q: A botanist randomly samples \(60\) oak trees across Pinewood Park and finds \(70\%\) have healthy bark. To which population can this result best generalize?
choices: All oak trees in Pinewood Park
questions.answer: **Answer:** All oak trees in Pinewood Park. Random samples generalize strictly to the population from which the sample was drawn.

questions.q: Two classes took the same exam. Class A has mean \(78\) and standard deviation \(4\); Class B has mean \(78\) and standard deviation \(11\). Which interpretation is valid?
choices: Class B scores are more spread out from \(78\) than Class A scores
Class B scored higher on average
Class A has a wider range than Class B
questions.answer: **Answer:** Class B scores are more spread out from \(78\) than Class A scores. Larger standard deviation indicates greater spread around the mean.

questions.q: A random sample of \(400\) shoppers finds \(46\%\) use reusable bags with margin of error \(5\%\). Which population percentage is plausible?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(49\%\). The plausible interval is \([41\%, 51\%]\); only \(49\%\) falls inside it.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A teacher recorded the number of questions answered correctly by eight students: 4, 8, 8, 12, 15, 15, 15, and 20. What is the mode of these scores?
questions.answer: The value 15 appears most frequently (3 times).

questions.q: Five distinct positive integers have median \(10\) and mean \(11\). What is the maximum possible value of the largest integer?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(31\). Total sum is \(55\). Minimize the remaining four distinct positive integers with 3rd equal to \(10\): \(1, 2, 10, 11\) sum to \(24\), so \(55 - 24 = 31\).

questions.q: Observing \(500\) adults, researchers notice people who walk daily sleep better. Why can this study NOT establish that walking causes better sleep?
choices: Participants were not randomly assigned to walking vs. non-walking groups
Sleep cannot be measured in hours
questions.answer: **Answer:** Participants were not randomly assigned to walking vs. non-walking groups. Without random assignment to treatment groups, confounding variables remain possible in an observational study.

questions.q: Which modification to a dataset guarantees zero change to its standard deviation?
questions.answer: **Answer:** Subtracting \(15\) from every data point. Subtracting a constant shifts center without changing distances between data points and the mean.

questions.q: Set M consists of \(\{2, 2, 6, 10, 10\}\). If we replace both \(2\)s and \(10\)s with \(5\)s and \(7\)s to form \(\{5, 5, 6, 7, 7\}\), how do mean and standard deviation change?
choices: Both mean and standard deviation stay unchanged
questions.answer: **Answer:** Mean stays \(6\); standard deviation decreases. Both symmetric sets average to \(6\), while values in \(\{5,5,6,7,7\}\) cluster much closer to \(6\).

questions.q: A city council reports average household water bill is \(74\) dollars, while median bill is \(52\) dollars. Which statement must be true?
choices: More than half of households pay over \(74\) dollars
Some households have exceptionally high bills pulling the mean upward
All households pay between \(52\) and \(74\) dollars
questions.answer: **Answer:** Some households have exceptionally high bills pulling the mean upward. Mean exceeding median indicates right skew from high-value outliers.

questions.q: What happens to the margin of error if a random sample is increased from \(400\) to \(1,600\) participants under identical sampling conditions?
choices: It is cut roughly in half
questions.answer: **Answer:** It is cut roughly in half. Margin of error scales inversely with \(\sqrt{n}\): multiplying \(n\) by \(4\) divides margin of error by \(\sqrt{4} = 2\).

questions.q: Seven workers earn a median salary of \(50\) thousand dollars. If the highest-paid worker gets a raise, how do the median and mean change?
choices: Median increases; mean stays the same
questions.answer: **Answer:** Median stays \(50\); mean increases. Raising the maximum only increases the sum (and thus the mean) without altering the 4th ordered salary.
